For a long-term DCA investor, the fundamentals remain compelling, but sizing discipline is warranted right now.

current.long_term_thesis: XLK provides concentrated, low-cost exposure to the largest and most profitable technology companies in the world — including Apple, Microsoft, and NVIDIA — which sit at the center of secular growth themes like artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and digital transformation. Over multi-year horizons, the technology sector has consistently been the primary driver of S&P 500 returns, making XLK a high-conviction core holding for long-term growth portfolios.
current.risks: Concentration risk is the primary concern — XLK's top 2-3 holdings (Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA) can represent 40–50%+ of the fund, meaning single-stock or single-theme shocks hit hard. Additionally, the 0.09% expense ratio (likely a data error showing 9.00% — verify this) is fine, but the valuation of the underlying holdings is stretched after a near-60% 1-year gain, making the fund vulnerable to sharp drawdowns if AI growth expectations disappoint, interest rates stay elevated, or a risk-off rotation into defensive sectors accelerates.

The ETF offers unmatched exposure to the secular technology megatrend through a liquid, well-established fund. Since it is not yet in the portfolio, begin building a position now at normal contribution size to establish a cost basis — but do not front-load.
